key_insight: Automatically generate personalized worked examples from students' actual code submissions by detecting recurring code patterns and mapping them to pattern-based knowledge components, enabling targeted remediation without heavy manual authoring.
problem_solved: Addresses the mismatch between fixed libraries of worked examples and the diverse partial solutions/errors students produce, reducing instructor authoring effort while delivering more relevant practice.
method: Mine student code submissions to detect recurring solution and error patterns.
Convert detected patterns into pattern-based knowledge components that represent target concepts and common misconceptions.
Assemble and generate worked examples tailored to a student's partial or incorrect code by applying the relevant knowledge components.
impact: Makes worked-example generation scalable and fine-grained, improving the relevance of feedback and practice in programming tutors while lowering content-creation costs — valuable for developers of intelligent tutoring systems and adaptive learning platforms.
visual_elements: Pipeline flowchart: Student code → Pattern detection → Knowledge components → Generated worked example
Side-by-side example: original student submission vs. tailored worked example highlighting corrected steps
Bar/line chart: improvements in coverage, time-to-feedback, or learning gains compared to fixed libraries
Icon set: pattern bank, automated generator, instructor savings, student learning boost
paper_title: Personalized Worked Example Generation from Student Code Submissions using Pattern-based Knowledge Components
paper_authors: Griffin Pitts, Muntasir Hoq, Peter Brusilovsky, Narges Norouzi, Arto Hellas
